record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How should workforce-scheduling algorithms for essential in-person work incorporate social distancing objectives, so that schedules reduce physical contacts or increase physical distance among employees at workplaces rather than optimizing mainly for operational cost, service level, urgency, skills, workload balance, or rotating shifts?

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that the main objective of these approaches is to minimize cost, which is not the highest priority in the context of social distancing.
Therefore, developing techniques to reduce the physical contacts or distance among employees at the workplace is critical for workforce scheduling in social distancing scenarios.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Formulate and solve a workforce-scheduling optimization problem for essential in-person work in which the primary objective explicitly incorporates social distancing. Specifically:

Setup. Let $E = \{1,\dots,n\}$ be a set of employees, $T = \{1,\dots,H\}$ a discrete planning horizon of shifts/time-slots, and $L = \{1,\dots,m\}$ a set of physical work locations (zones) of a workplace, each with capacity $c_\ell$ and a layout that determines a pairwise distance $d_{\ell}(i,j)$ between any two employees co-located in zone $\ell$. Each employee $i$ has skills $S_i$, availability $A_i \subseteq T$, and demanded workload; each task at $(\ell,t)$ has skill, urgency, and staffing requirements. A schedule is an assignment $x_{i,\ell,t}\in\{0,1\}$ satisfying coverage, skill, capacity, availability, workload-balance, and shift-rotation constraints.

Define a contact measure $C(x) = \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\sum_{i\neq j} x_{i,\ell,t}\,x_{j,\ell,t}\,\mathbf{1}\!\left[d_\ell(i,j)<\delta\right]$ for a threshold $\delta>0$, and a distance measure $D(x) = \sum_{t,\ell,i\neq j} x_{i,\ell,t}x_{j,\ell,t}\,d_\ell(i,j)$.

Problem. Design a scheduling algorithm whose objective is to minimize $C(x)$ (or maximize $D(x)$, or a weighted combination) subject to all the operational constraints above, rather than primarily minimizing operating cost. In particular:

(a) Give a precise mathematical programming or constraint-programming formulation that supports staggered shifts, zone assignments, and break scheduling, in which physical-contact reduction is the lexicographically first or top-weighted objective.

(b) Provide an exact or approximation algorithm with provable guarantees on $C(x)$ (or $D(x)$) under the feasibility constraints, or prove hardness and give a tractable heuristic.

(c) Quantify the trade-off frontier between contact reduction and traditional criteria (cost, service level, urgency satisfaction, skill match, workload balance, fairness of rotations), e.g., by characterizing the Pareto front.

The goal is a scheduling framework whose schedules demonstrably reduce physical contacts or increase pairwise physical distance among employees at the workplace, with rigorous guarantees, instead of treating social distancing as a soft side-constraint to a cost-minimization objective.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originally posed as an open direction, has been partially addressed by subsequent work proposing constraint-optimization models that incorporate worker physical-distancing requirements into workforce scheduling and study trade-offs with production performance (e.g., a 2022 model in International Journal of Production Research / Production & Manufacturing Research). However, no general framework with provable guarantees and a complete Pareto-trade-off characterization across all stated criteria appears established, so the broader problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: How to front the physical distancing requirement within workforce scheduling: empirical investigation through an optimization model
status_evidence.snippet: Constraint optimization model considering social distancing of workers as part of workforce scheduling requirements; investigates how workforce distancing affects production performance.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent research has formulated workforce-scheduling optimization models that explicitly incorporate physical-distancing constraints/objectives, partially addressing the question.
